content.title: What are Arrays and Methods?
content.description: Arrays allow you to store multiple values of the same data type in a single variable, while methods are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks.

content.content: As programs grow larger, managing data and avoiding repetitive code become important. Arrays help organize collections of similar data, while methods improve code reusability, readability, and modularity.

content.title: Why Learn Arrays & Methods?
content.content: Arrays efficiently store collections of data, and methods reduce duplicate code by allowing logic to be written once and reused multiple times.

content.title: Arrays and Methods Overview
steps: Store Multiple Values in an Array

content.content: Introduction to Arrays
An array is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations. Each element is accessed using its index, starting from 0.
Array Initialization
Arrays can be initialized either by specifying the size or by providing values directly during declaration.

content.title: Remember
content.content: Array indices always begin with 0. Accessing an invalid index causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Traversing an Array
Traversal means visiting every element in an array. This is commonly done using a for loop or an enhanced for-each loop.

content.title: Array Traversal

content.content: Enhanced for Loop
The enhanced for loop (for-each loop) simplifies array traversal when the index value is not required.

content.title: Enhanced for Loop

content.content: Introduction to Methods
A method is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task. Instead of writing the same code multiple times, we write it once inside a method and call it whenever needed.

content.title: Simple Method
Method Components
content.description: A method consists of an access modifier, return type, method name, parameters (optional), and method body.

content.content: Method Parameters and Return Values
Methods can receive input using parameters and return results using the return statement.

content.title: Method with Parameters

content.content: Method Types

items.question: Method with Parameters
items.answer: Accepts input values from the caller.

items.question: Method with Return Value
items.answer: Returns a computed result back to the caller.

items.question: Void Method
items.answer: Performs an action but does not return any value.

content.content: Passing Arrays to Methods
Arrays can be passed as arguments to methods, allowing multiple values to be processed efficiently inside reusable functions.

content.title: Passing an Array

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Classroom Attendance
content.content: An array is like a classroom attendance register that stores the names of all students in one place. A method is like the teacher who performs tasks such as counting students or marking attendance whenever required.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Questions about arrays, array traversal, method creation, parameter passing, return types, and passing arrays to methods are frequently asked in Java interviews.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Why does ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException occur?
items.answer: Because the program tries to access an index outside the valid range of the array.

items.question: Why must a non-void method return a value?
items.answer: Because the declared return type requires a value to be returned.

items.question: What is a common mistake while traversing arrays?
items.answer: Using <= instead of < with the array length, causing an invalid index access.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use arrays to store collections of similar data and methods to organize reusable logic into smaller, manageable blocks.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Arrays store multiple values of the same data type.
Methods can accept parameters and return values.
Arrays can be passed as arguments to methods.
